subject: FintechCorp - Security discovery follow-up: incident response, breach notification & BCP evidence
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sam Williams <sam.williams@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-20T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: FintechCorp - Security discovery follow-up: incident response, breach notification & BCP evidence

Hi Sam / Aisha,

Thanks again for the time this morning — good discussion and appreciate the level of detail your security team provided. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Call recap:
- SOC 2: you asked about our current certification status and timing for Type II coverage.
- Incident response: you requested our IR timelines and notification commitments to customers and regulators.
- BCP/DR: you asked for evidence of recent DR tests, RTO/RPO targets, and runbooks.
- Vendor questionnaire: please send the link or portal; we will begin filling this out immediately.

What we are sharing now (attached/stubbed):
- IR_playbook_v2.pdf (overview of our incident response process and escalation matrix).
- DR_test_report_20261112.pdf (summary of the most recent DR exercise).
- High-level architecture diagram and data flow (will share on Drive link below).

High-level answers to get us started:
- SOC 2: Redwood currently holds SOC 2 Type I as of 2026-10-01. We are in the process of completing Type II coverage; expected report issuance is 2027-04-30. If helpful, we can provide a bridge letter and our SOC 2 Type I report today.
- Breach notification: Redwood commits to notifying customers and affected stakeholders within 24 hours of a confirmed customer-impacting data breach, with status updates every 48 hours thereafter until resolution. We can provide our notification templates and regulatory escalation playbook.
- BCP/DR: our production inference platform RTO target is 4 hours for core serving paths; RPO target is under 1 hour for customer-critical data. Last full DR exercise was 2026-11-12 (report attached).

Requests / next steps:
1) Sam — please share the vendor security questionnaire link and any deadline you have.
2) We will populate the questionnaire and target an initial submission by 2027-01-27.
3) We can run through any follow-up technical deep-dive next week; propose Tue/Wed afternoon PT.

Attachments: IR_playbook_v2.pdf (PDF, 850KB)
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d5e6f

Best,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

From: Sam Williams <sam.williams@fintechcorp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Khan <ciso@fintechcorp.com>, security@fintechcorp.com
Date: 2027-01-20T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FintechCorp - Security discovery follow-up: incident response, breach notification & BCP evidence

Jordan — thanks for the quick recap and for the attachments. A few clarifying items from our side: 

1) Breach notification timing: our legal/regulatory team will need to know the maximum time window Redwood commits to after detection vs confirmation. Can you confirm whether Redwood's 24-hour commitment is from detection or from confirmation of customer-impacting scope? Also, what's your cadence for regulator/customer notifications and who is the point of contact?

2) RTO/RPO: please confirm which services the 4 hour RTO covers (inference API, admin console, data plane, etc.). We need explicit RTO/RPO per component for our risk model.

3) DR evidence: appreciate the DR test report stub. Can you confirm whether the test included an automated failover to the alternate region and whether a full data failover was performed? Also who ran the test (internal ops vs third party auditor).

4) Vendor questionnaire: we are using our vendor portal. Please start here: https://fintechcorp.sharepoint.com/sites/vendor-security/questionnaire/12345 and aim to complete by EOD Thursday (2027-01-27).

5) Logs/audit trail: we will need retention windows for audit logs and where they are stored (KMS, customer-key support).

If you can get the above answers and the SOC 2 artifacts by Thursday, that will keep our procurement timeline moving.

Thanks,
Sam Williams
Security Program Manager
FintechCorp
sam.williams@fintechcorp.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sam Williams <sam.williams@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-20T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FintechCorp - Security discovery follow-up: incident response, breach notification & BCP evidence

Sam — great questions. Answers below, and happy to expand with a technical screen-share if helpful.

1) Breach notification timing:
- Redwood defines an incident as detection -> assessment -> confirmation. Our customer notification SLA is 24 hours from confirmation of customer-impacting data exposure. We typically notify customers within 24 hours of confirmation, and provide substantive status updates every 48 hours until resolved. For regulatory filings, we will coordinate with your legal team and provide the timeline and artifacts needed for filing. Point of contact for notifications: incident@redwood.com and jordan.blake@redwood.com (cc'd).

2) RTO/RPO by component (high-level):
- Inference API (public endpoints): RTO target = 4 hours; RPO = < 1 hour for customer-critical state.
- Control plane / admin console: RTO target = 12 hours; RPO = < 4 hours.
- Telemetry / metrics pipeline: best-effort for non-critical metrics; core alerts are routed to on-call within minutes.

3) DR test details:
- The 2026-11-12 exercise included an automated failover of stateless serving to an alternate region and a manual failover of persistent KV stores. The runbook and summary are in DR_test_report_20261112.pdf. The test was run by our internal SRE team with third-party observation from SecureOps Consulting.

4) Vendor questionnaire:
- We will begin the portal submission today and target initial responses by 2027-01-27. If you need an exec summary sooner, Marissa will provide a one-pager.

5) Logs/audit trail & KMS:
- Audit logs retained for 13 months by default; retention can be extended under contract. Logs are stored in encrypted buckets with access controlled via IAM and customer-key options are available via AWS KMS. Ben is copied to surface any additional artefacts.

Attachments: DR_test_report_20261112.pdf
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d5e6f

Let us know if you want to schedule a technical deep dive — Jordan and our SRE (Ben) can join.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

I will aim to have the summary and the questionnaire initial submission by EOD Thursday (2027-01-27).

Marissa Cole
